The middle of awareness is marked by a certain relation of support and supported, arising through the differentiation of the principles and the standing of each in its own nature.

quick_english: Because he was made clear earlier in relation to the hells, he is regarded as below them; the mighty one's flame extends ten crores, and above it there is an empty space of half that extent.
Above that level stand the lords of hell, feeling only pain in graded order, with some in the middle and others above, surrounded by intervals of difference.
Among them, in order, are avici, kumbhipaka, and raurava, eleven and eleven and ten, ending at arrow-fire.
For each of these there is a crore height interval, a lakh measure, and a duration between sky-void mouth counts.
Above kushmanda, those who perform dark action contrary to scripture are placed in a lakh-less-crore station.
There, terrible world-persons torment them until enjoyment ends, except those who once took refuge in supreme Shiva with one-pointed mind.
They do not go hell-yoked; their dark result gives only small pleasure, with thousand-nine heights and one interval following in order.
In the eight patalas, one each, Hatuka is lord in the eighth; Shrikantha appoints selves per world and forces many.
Thus that one gives powers in the raurava rule to vow-keepers and those who perform forbidden conduct.
Even initiated persons who lose their vow and do not perform penances become corrupters of left conduct in that place.
Those living by shares of god, fire, and substance stand highest; others below are devoted to garuda and other mantras.
They are various servants before Hatuka; but if there they worship the god-lord with devotion, they are transformed.
They dissolve in that lord-principle and gradually reach supreme Shiva; otherwise they remain engaged in that enjoyment.
They, devoted to crying under time-fire torment, dissolve in the quality-principle and then return again at creation's mouth.
They are cast by mothers with terrible torment into lowest-low bodies, according to their own action.
Among humans there, some mantra-knowers are freed in order, but others are bound according to prior deed.
Thus this group account, named hulahula and so on, is spoken by the blessed one in the shrimad ananda-adhika rule.
Above patala are thousands and twenty earth-bowl; in siddha tantra, on patala's back, it is surrounded by yakshi.
Adepts play with them at Bhadrakali's city; then dark hot earth, then void, then horse.
These are torment places for corrupters of guru-mantra and the like; then above earth and middle to Meru, thousands and sixteen.
Its root is submerged and spread, its height is thousand-ocean-vasu, and it is the golden abode of all gods.
Middle-above-below is a risen arrow-bowl square; Bhairavi and that linga are named, and earth is its pedestal.
All gods are indeed dissolved there; that is always worshipped in the middle, in the Meru assembly, with element and lord-direction banner.
Shambhu's light-peak and Shrikantha's part are that lord; descending, thousands and fourteen of Manovati.
Here at Meru is a four-direction circle-wall; world-guardians are placed east and south of Amaravati's center.

quick_english: On the left side of Meru stand two white-peaked mountains, and between them lies Hiranmaya, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is twelve and a half.
There, to the left, between the Shveta and Nila mountains, lies Ramyaka, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is twelve.
South of Meru are the mountains Hema and Nishadha, and between them lies Harivarsha, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is a thousand more.
Farther south, between Hema and Himavat, lies Kimpurusha, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is a thousand more.
South of Himavat lies Bharata, nine thousand in extent, the lowest land where beings both perform action and experience its fruits.
Ilavrita, Ketubhadra, Kuru, Hairanya, Ramyaka, and the regions of Hari and Kimpurusha are lands of enjoyment, but not lands of action.
In those regions, although they are mainly not lands of action, even animals may acquire karmic impressions because of firmly established prior conditioning.
Even beings without present impressions may appear in Bharata or elsewhere, and through firm prior impressions or by the Lord's will they may still experience good and bad results.
Action is also found in other places, as the ancient tradition says; there the time is always Treta, but in Bharata the full cycle of four ages prevails.
In Bharata there are nine divisions separated by ocean water; the land measures five hundred and the water measures five hundred as well.
The divisions are Indra, Kasheru, Tamrabha, Naga, eastern Gabhastimat, Saumya, Gandharva, Varaha, and the one called Kanya, extending up to the ocean.
In the ninth division, Kanya island, there are six sub-islands situated to the south in the middle of the ocean, and the island is adorned by seven chief mountains.
The mountains are Anga, Yava, Malaya, Shanku, Kumuda, and Varaha; Agastya dwells on Malaya, and Lanka stands on Trikuta—these are the six sub-islands.
The islands and sub-islands are inhabited mostly by various foreign peoples and are rich in pearls, gold, and gems, as stated in the teaching of Shri Ruru.
Whatever action is done in Bharata can be exhausted there, and by it one may reach from the lowest hell up to Shiva, or even attain liberation—especially in the region called Kanya.
In Bharata dwell Mahakala and a crore of Rudras, and there flow the Ganga and five hundred other sacred streams; therefore birth here is extremely hard to obtain.
In other regions beings pass through their karma by mere enjoyment, like animals, but for those born in Bharata even attainments beyond desire are possible.

Svayambhuva Manu had ten sons; later three departed, and in the land called Jambu the king was Agnidhra.
Agnidhra had nine sons, and from them came the ninefold division; Nabhi was the ninth, and his grandson was Bharata, the son of Rishabha.
Bharata had eight sons and one daughter, making a ninth share; they divided and enjoyed that territory of one lakh yojanas in nine parts.

quick_english: It is also the abode of vidyadharas, and in short, for the whole creation of beings it serves as a place of enjoyment and residence according to their desire.
Between bhuvarloka and the sun there are ten wind paths, each separated by ten thousand units.
The first wind path above is ritarddhi, fifty yojanas above.
The nourishing wind is followed by pracetas, higher by a hundred.
Mute lightning clouds stand a krosa from earth and shower rain.
Above them are clouds showering frogs and beings, and higher poison-water clouds.
Skanda-born clouds and pisacas occur in the flood wind; fifty above are maraka clouds.
Mahadeva-born vinayakas there take away the actions of unperfected men.
Fifty above is vajranka wind, with stone clouds and lowest vidyadharas.
Those who died with siddhi are situated in vajranka wind.
Fifty above vajranka are electric rain clouds, apsarasas, and merit-doing men.
Those who died in these circumstances are situated in the electric level.
After the electric level come nourishment clouds, disease-water clouds, and samvartas.
In raivata there is a place for anger-water releasers, and visavarta is that wind.
Fifty above are storm clouds and fire-born vidyadhara specialists who worship the supreme lord.
A hundred above visavarta is durjaya, the breath-born.
Paravaha contains brahma clouds, pushkara clouds, wind-goers, and gandharvas.
Avaha contains jimuta clouds, highest vidyadharas, and form-vow worlds.
Mahavaha has beings-benefiting clouds, and mahaparivaha has skull-born clouds of mahesha.
At the end of mahaparivaha is ritarddhi, with eastern wind path, fire daughters, and mothers established by rudra power.
The second level has siddhas and caranas, the fourth has divine weapons and direction elephants, and the fifth is noted.
The sixth level has garuda, bull, and lord, with daksha; the ninth is established by brahma power.
The tenth wind path contains vasus, rudras, and adityas, and the sun's orb is nine thousand yojanas.
Svarga loka is defined from bhuvarloka to the end of dhruva, with knowledge power shining as the lord's sun.
Cool-rayed action power of shiva is a lakh from the sun, stellar is a lakh from the moon, then two lakhs.

From the earth up to Saturn, the wise know a set of five planets, each at its own interval. From the sun, the realm of the Seven Sages is one lakh away, and from there the Pole Star is placed at the same distance.
The unmoving Pole Star is Brahma himself in a lower form, stationed in Brahma's place. It has become the central pivot of all celestial cars and stands above them all.
Here, all things are understood to be bound within the sphere of wind. There are seven heavenly wind masses, chiefly beginning with the clouds and the like.
Those who perform sacrifices and other rites but lack knowledge go to heaven. When that merit is exhausted, they return to the human world because of the merit that still remains.
Thus, from the earth up to the Pole Star the distance is fifteen lakhs. From heaven up to the Great World it is two crores and eighty-five lakhs.
In the Great World dwell seers, sages, and perfected beings such as Markandeya. Gods whose duties have come to an end also abide there.
In the great intermediate space there are others who still hold office. Eight crores above the Great World is the Jana world, where Kapila and others dwell.
Many happy Sadhyas dwell there as well. One crore above the Jana world is the Tapas world, where Sanaka and others of great wisdom reside.
There the lords of creatures born from Brahma hold their office. Above the Tapas world, sixteen crores away, is Satya, the abode of Brahma.
There the self-born Brahma dwells and manifests this universe. In the Satya world are the Vedas and others who have been refined by action and meditation.
There, above, one crore higher, are those established in bliss at Brahma's seat. Two crores above Brahma's seat is the city of Vishnu.
Devotees of Vishnu reach that abode through meditation, worship, and recitation. Seven crores above Vishnu's world is the world of the supreme lord.
Rudra is the maker of creation and dissolution within the cosmic egg. Those who are devoted to worship of the linga but lack initiation and knowledge are connected with his realm.
They go to Rudra's city within the cosmic egg and never fall back down. All who dwell there eventually go to Shiva, becoming Rudras initiated by Srikantha.
When their office comes to an end, they ascend together with the group of Rudra's daughters, going from city to city above Rudra in ever higher stages.
Below the cosmic egg and above Rudra is the city of the staff-bearer. By Shiva's will he holds the egg firm and also opens the path of liberation.
Sharva, Rudra, Bhima, Bhava, Ugra, the great lord, and Ishana are the seven Shiva-lords of the worlds, ruling upward from the earth world.
Seven worlds are formed from gross particulars, while the higher worlds are formed from subtle ones. The teacher explained this clearly in the Ruru scripture.
In Brahma's first creation, five gross particulars called the abundant ones were made from his own body. With a seventh formed from them, these became the basis of the seven worlds.
Beyond that, the worlds are supported by subtle coverings: great elements born from the tanmatras, upheld through subtle bodies and mutually connected by smell and the other subtle qualities.
From the fire of time up to the staff-bearer the distance is eighty-eight crores. Above that, within the cosmic egg, is a solid shell one crore yojanas thick.
There are fifty crores above the earth's surface and fifty crores below, making the earth sphere one hundred crores in all. From that it is pictured like a golden grain of rice.
The mantra extending to the hundred Rudras, with the syllables hum and phat, splits that hard-to-pacify boundary. Ten by ten in every direction, there are a hundred Rudras outside.
That which supports the cosmic egg does so by its own power on all sides. The teachers, in the Raurava and other scriptures, have said that it has the form of an egg.

quick_english: One might object that powers immersed in Shiva should also be eggs, but they are not, because they have not fallen from their own state of power.
Another clarifying term is used so that egg-ness is not wrongly extended to bodies and sense bases, because nothing is inserted into them in that way.

quick_english: If bodies and sense bases form a collectivity, their oneness is explained by the word 'undivided', which shows that they share the same kind.
Someone might think that, even without using the term 'mass of reality', each principle by itself could have the nature of an egg; but the text challenges that idea.
Egg-nature would wrongly extend to a principle made only of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements; but the word 'reality' here means the whole made of bodies, sense bases, and worlds.

quick_english: Others say the distinguishing terms were used to prevent egg-ness from being misapplied; in any case, beyond the Brahma egg described here there are one hundred Rudras.
Over those hundred Rudras stand eleven radiant Rudra-lords of their own: Ananta, Kapalin, Agni, Yama, Nairrita, Bala, and the rest named in sequence.
The remaining Rudra-lords are Shighra, Nidhisha, Vidyesha, Shambhu, and Virabhadra; they surround the Brahma egg like bees covering honey and clusters of kadamba filaments.
In the same way, the Shiva-Rudras, with countless attendants, surround the Brahma egg; their arrangement is described in vast numbers, such as forty niyutas and a crore.
Presided over by Shrikantha, these Rudras create and withdraw, and they hold lordship over the gods, as stated in the Raurava Vartika.
But in the Siddha Tantra, beyond a hundred crores from the golden egg, there is a sequence of a hundred more eggs, successively doubled and associated with silver and other substances.
In those eggs, Brahmas exist in sequence with doubled lifespans; they perish in order, and at the end of that series a higher principle is reached.
From earth upward come water and the rest in order; up to ego the scale increases tenfold, and beyond that intellect increases a hundredfold.
Above intellect, manifest nature is a thousandfold, purusha is ten thousandfold, and niyati is a hundred thousandfold, leading to a millionfold beyond it.
Up to kala the scale is ten millionfold, Maya is a hundred millionfold, Ishvara is a billionfold, and beyond that it reaches a thousand crores.
Sadakhya pervades at that vast scale, and together with its multitude of powers the all-pervading goddess is established as pervading the entire path.
Beyond all that is the pure, supreme, immeasurable Shiva principle; from water up to Shiva-tattva, no one but Shiva has truly seen it.
For that reason, knowledge of Shiva is the supreme cause of liberation, as Mahadeva declares in the revered Svacchanda scripture.

quick_english: A bound soul does not attain liberation by hundreds of other kinds of knowledge; knowledge of Shiva does not arise without receiving Shaiva initiation.
The former supreme power, and the human-made one too, again grants blue-radiant victory above the hundred rudras, associated with Bhadrakali.
Kali's victorious city is not attainable by sacrifice, gift, or austerity; her devotees, well initiated in her circle, go there.
The supreme goddess gives liberation through seedless initiation; she performs for people as much initiation as corresponds to the vidyesha veil.
Those placed in this world attain a corresponding state; then Virabhadra, shining like end-of-age fire, appears by crores.
Those who remember the great lord and die in water, desert, fire, or by beheading reach his city called Vijaya.
They go to knowledge-Ishana and radiant Virabhadra, in a region spread by crores above Virabhadra, in three ways.
The water-bearing rudra egg, bow-shaped, is situated from Virabhadra's world and likewise from Bhadrakali's abode.
Adorned by thirteen other worlds, then earth with its mountain is defined by holding the smell tanmatra.
The dead go to that supreme earth; the wise go to the ocean city, attainable by holding the taste tanmatra.
Then Shri's city is reached in Rudra's play descents, especially by special death at Prayaga and Shri mountain.
Sarasvati city is the abode of knowers of sound-Brahman; those suitable to Rudra are situated there, while others stand apart from Rudras due to primacy.
In many cities Ganga, Shri, and Sarasvati appear; god-lords range from Lakula to Amarasha, with eight in the waters.
Then the fiery principle is the abode of Shiva-fire here; those who have resorted to fiery holding go to this fire.
In the fiery principle there are eight leaders from Bhairava to Hari; breath has a world, and air is divided in ten ways.
Having meditated or abandoned breaths and made holding there, great souls enter that, becoming air and sky-bodied.
The eight from Bhima to Gaya go to the air principle; the sky world is attainable by holding that space.
From cloth-foot-end to pillar-etc and eight gods are in the space principle; uninitiated beings claiming the Shiva principle are among beings.
Even those lacking knowledge, despite strong holding, go outside from the egg; earth, ocean, fire, air, and space goers, and initiated ones too, are named.
For the purpose of purification yoga, the supreme state is not sought in such descents, even for those who die in shrines.
Having attained that state, they gradually go to Shiva-nature; this is said again in the Shrimad Devi Tantra.
In the Shri Kamika's Kashmir description the lord has said that those who die in the great abode of the goddess die in that city.
Brahmins and mixed castes, beings up to immobile forms, and Rudra classes are these; thus says Lord Shiva.
Dear one, the cities of tanmatras through mind lie above the sky veil and below ego, in Shiva's doctrine.
The great smell-tanmatra circle, joined with five colors, is situated between, covered by many crores of yojanas.

quick_english: In each cosmic age that great goddess is described by different names; the city of the lord of Uma is then surrounded by the Mothers.
Shrikantha is the supreme form, and attendant goddesses such as Brahmi, Skandaja, Hari, Varahi, Indri, Viccika, and Carcika are named.
Yellow, white, yellow-blue, blue, and white-red are assigned in order to the corresponding directional goddesses.
By portion, the creator descends some goddesses into the human world, while other supreme ones remain established in the sky.
Those goddesses serve self-willed, because above the city of Uma's lord stands the supreme eight-fold form.
From those whose creation begins with Sharva and earth, the Ishana form is established on Meru.
Shrikantha pervades the world through eight bodies, and restrained devotees worship Shambhu's qualified yoga.
By seeing that circle, one is freed from duality, the three are removed, and the gunas are established in purity and impurity.
Because of gradation and difference in yoga, the fruits are varied, and this difference is called difference in enjoyment and attainment.
Above the eight forms, twelve radiant saffron forms are declared, ranging from Vama to Eka Shiva.
Above that stands Virabhadra, lord of the circle; one who attains sayujya delights together with him.
From the eight divine wombs to the thumb-sized end, eight Mahadevas may be, and this intellect principle is declared.
At the end of the eight Mahadevas, the eight yoga is declared here; there Shrikantha, lord of Uma, is declared.
Auspicious forms, the hero, the eight Mahadevas, and the body are named; nature's gunas are above and below intellect.
There agitated gunas produce intellect; inequality not attained is not a cause for producing effects.
Nature may be cause through guna equilibrium, but without agitation it still has unequal gunas.
How would instability arise in the first agitation? This is Sankhya's fault, if by that those gunas.
The unmanifest is desired; equilibrium is mere contact, not otherwise, and our view joins it with the independent lord's will agitation.
The unmanifest is cause of intellect principle; agitated gunas are involved, and nature's agitation comes from the lord's will before.
That indeed may be the intellect principle; what need of other imagined gunas? It is not obstructed by cause-form reflection.
Then other agitation produces effects like seed and sprout, and rows of heavy ones are established in tamas, rajas, and sattva.
Three, thirty-two, one, thirty-one, and twenty-one are listed; by their own knowledge, yoga, and power, the best teachers play.
Three-eyed ones, freed from bonds, do grace; intellect and guna extend to both, seven more than a hundred.
Among Rudras and worlds, chiefly others, the eight yoga is declared between them, in the guna mass and again in Shiva's body.
Having transcended the womb, in the secondary mass, yoga givers would be unmade, made, vibhu, Virincha, Hari, Guha, and then goddess by order.

tokens.grounds: instruments and qualities such as aṇimā
sattva and the rest belonging to them

quick_english: From the unmanifest arise the organs, the subtle powers like smallness, the effects, the manifold of cognitions, and the qualities beginning with sattva.

tokens.grounds: the four qualities dharma, jñāna, virāga, aiśvarya

quick_english: These givers of yoga, arising from the qualities, bestow on souls merit, knowledge, dispassion, lordship, and their various fruits.

tokens.grounds: of the deity whose seat is the guṇas beginning with sattva
of the lord who is the consort of the sole mother of the entire universe

quick_english: Beyond them is the world of the god Śrīkaṇṭhanātha, who is seated on the qualities beginning with sattva and is the lord and consort of the one mother of the entire universe.

tokens.grounds: by whom, in the worlds of Umā, Guha, Nīla, Brahmā, Ṛbhukṣa, Kṛta, Akṛta, and others
in the form of a graha or seizing power
ruling over Prabhū and other beings

quick_english: By his power, taking a seizing form, he presides over the beings in the worlds of Umā, Guha, Nīla, Brahmā, Ṛbhukṣa, Kṛta, Akṛta, and others.

tokens.grounds: who, entering the lotus of the four-faced Brahmā
burns the four worlds and again creates the worlds of people

quick_english: When he wishes to withdraw the worlds, he enters the lotus of the four-faced Brahmā, burns the four worlds, and then creates the human worlds again.

tokens.grounds: whose body consists of the guṇas beginning with sattva
there she is worshiped in every cycle

quick_english: By his will, Rudrāṇī, whose body consists of the qualities beginning with sattva, brings forth in each cycle, and there she is worshiped at the altar in every cycle.

tokens.grounds: then by Paśupati, Indra, Upendra, and Viriñci
and likewise varied rites are performed by gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, ancestors, and sages

quick_english: Then, in connection with that attainment, Paśupati, Indra, Upendra, Viriñci, the gods, and also gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, ancestors, and sages perform varied sacrifices.

tokens.grounds: the deities Krodheśa, Caṇḍa, and Saṃvarta

quick_english: The supreme equilibrium of the qualities is the unmanifest. Above the level of the qualities are Krodheśa, Caṇḍa, Saṃvarta, Jyotiḥ, Piṅgala, and Sūraka.
There are Pañcāntaka, Ekavīra, and Śikhin, making eight. There that principle is the dense resting place of the soul, prakṛti, the root, pradhāna, the unmanifest.

tokens.grounds: thus these are called the cause of the guṇas
of that which is born from māyā
whose minds are tainted by both innate and adventitious impurity

quick_english: These are synonymous names for the cause of the qualities, belonging to what arises from māyā; all the embodied knowers whose minds are stained by innate and adventitious impurity are there.

tokens.grounds: those who enjoy the experiences arising from it
with faculties that are deluded, manifest, or dissolved

quick_english: All of them are established there, along with Rudras who enjoy the experiences arising from it. Some have faculties that are deluded, manifest, or dissolved, while others are without faculties.

tokens.grounds: due to not having been brought under presiding control

quick_english: In the teaching, faculties that are not yet governed and cannot act are called deluded, while those that clearly grasp their fixed objects are called unfolded.

tokens.grounds: at the time of universal dissolution
and the effect is to be understood in the same way

quick_english: At the great dissolution they are broken and dissolved; at creation they are not yet produced. Dependent on will, they are again called without faculties, and the same is true of their effects.

tokens.grounds: at the level of the puruṣa tattva
prior to that or in front of that
just the eight worlds beginning with aṇimā

quick_english: At the level of the puruṣa principle there are the nine satisfactions, the eight accomplishments, and likewise the eight worlds beginning with aṇimā.

tokens.grounds: in what is not truly the tattva
through the cognition that it is a tattva
a cognition of acceptability even in what should be rejected

quick_english: When what is not the true principle is taken as a principle, the resulting contentment is called satisfaction. Taking what should be rejected as acceptable is called accomplishment, as the Kāpilas say.

tokens.grounds: called prakṛti, upādāna, kāla, and bhāgya
five arise from cessation regarding objects through gain, protection, association, loss, and obstruction

quick_english: Four satisfactions are internal, named prakṛti, acquisition, time, and fortune. Five arise from turning away from objects through gain, protection, association, loss, and obstruction.

tokens.grounds: the earlier obstacle to accomplishment is threefold

quick_english: Reasoning, scriptural word, and study are three means that remove suffering; gaining friends and giving are also included, making the eight accomplishments. The obstacle before accomplishment is threefold.

tokens.grounds: above aṇimā and the rest there are three
because of association with the reflection of the three guṇas

quick_english: Above the worlds beginning with aṇimā there are three rows connected with teacher and disciple. Their threefold division is explained by the influence of the three qualities.

tokens.grounds: beginning with iḍā and so on

quick_english: Above those rows is the eightfold set of nāḍī-knowledges beginning with iḍā. In the soul there is established a power made of sound, called expansion.

tokens.grounds: for one who is not an agent
the puruṣa cannot have the status of an agent
the state of being a cause

quick_english: A soul that is not an agent cannot truly be established as the doer. Even if the soul is not an agent, it may still stand as an assisting cause.

tokens.grounds: otherwise one would have to accept that it becomes the rest of the effect
since that would negate the doctrine that the effect pre-exists

quick_english: Otherwise one would have to treat the soul as part of the effect, which would undermine the doctrine that the effect pre-exists. Therefore, in such a case, there is a specific power belonging to the soul.

tokens.grounds: the eightfold set of forms is now spoken of

quick_english: Taking on that many forms, that power attains fullness. Above the eight nāḍīs, an eightfold set of forms is taught.

tokens.grounds: what is to be done or produced
knowledge and the instruments that accomplish it
the eightfold set in the form of embodied pairs
at the level of the puruṣa tattva

quick_english: At the level of the puruṣa principle there is an eightfold embodied set: effect, cause, suffering, pleasure, knowledge, what is to be accomplished, the instruments, and the means.

tokens.grounds: of the bodily observances or qualities
brahmacarya, absence of deceit, and absence of anger

quick_english: Beyond the eightfold forms is the world of the ten bodily observances: non-harm, truth, non-stealing, continence, freedom from deceit, freedom from anger, and duties toward the teacher.
In the principle of the person are the ten declared qualities, including service, purity, contentment, and straightness. There too is situated a sixteenfold set ending with smell.
Starting from the world called the body-bond, the qualities of intellect appear. There the ego is present in eightfold and threefold forms, along with bonds beginning with desire.
The bonds are threefold: adventitious, of the Ganeshas, and of the Vidyeshvaras. They are present in the person and block the path to liberation.
Whatever is other than the supreme Shiva, whose nature is nondual consciousness, freedom, and beauty, is called a bond.
Thus, even though the supreme Lord remains full, when personhood is assumed there arises a wondrous non-recognition of his own nature; from that come persons.
All the bonds, whether stated or unstated and described in the Paratantra, are present in the person. By purifying them there, one is freed from worldly becoming.
Above the person, in niyati, dwell ten Shankaras, golden and very white. In the principle of time dwell ten Shivas.
In raga is the world of Viresha, a city of teachers and students, with ten million and sixteen thousand attendants for each.
In impure knowledge there is a world shining with nine Shaktis, beginning with Vama and extending up to Manonmani.
In kala is the supreme world of the three great gods. Beyond that is maya, a threefold domain filled chiefly with countless millions.
That maya is pervaded by cavities called bhaga, as taught in the Shaiva scripture. Again, there is a group of eight great gods extending to the measure of a thumb at night.
Likewise, in the teaching of Shrimalini, the powers beginning with Vama are described as ruling the eight circles; in the earlier sacred teaching they are said to begin from the level of the person.
In the Shaiva scripture they are placed in the principle of maya, under Ananta: skull-vow observers, those who offer their own limbs, and practitioners of harsh austerities.
Fearless and observing the sword-edge vow, knowing the principles, they gradually ascend through each principle until they reach the place where the lord is called Ananta.
And it is said that beyond him is the abode of the lord of Ananta, the god who performs creation, maintenance, and dissolution, and who guards the door of the cave and the bhaga.
Drawing them out again and again from the cavity of maya, he bestows on persons merits, powers such as minuteness, knowledges, austerities, pleasures, and yogic attainments.
Empowered by his energy, all the lords from Ananta onward, down to those beginning with Shatabhava, shine like lamps dispelling darkness in the office of the cave.
Presiding over the unmanifest, Shiva brings forth the world by the command of Shambhu, because he is the cause of authority over both the pure and impure streams.
Those first established in that great station endowed with Shiva's qualities, beginning with Ananta, become the agents of the world's creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
This has been called the cavity of maya. Beyond it is the cave, the womb of the world, where generation occurs as the stirring of the lord's power takes effect.
In the womb-openings, rich with various desires and called bhaga, when the lord desires the goddess who follows his will, the generative process begins.
In each bhaga, offspring beginning with the unmanifest are born from her. They are so extremely subtle that their nature is not described in the prescribed texts.
Just as many enclosed inner rooms can exist within one hall, so many womb-cavities exist within the single head-hall of maya.
Covered by subtle layers and walls of maya, invisible to one another, countless happy Rudras dwell there in each cavity.
Dwellers in each world are taught by teachers as having attained union, proximity, or supreme same-world residence.
Even words of the accomplished, uttered long ago, are worn out; numbers of streams are not spoken again from endless rebirth.
Therefore, from one hell up to door guardians, other streams too are similarly arranged and to be known.
In unmanifest time, by cave, nature, and art, the own modification is woven across and through, pervaded, measured, full, and encircled.
In the middle, three sheaths of that contain rudras: six in the lower interval, one above, and five; these twelve are determined.
The deep difficult lords, hari, hara, dasha lords, and three-time lords; these six in the endless middle are auspicious brahman-lord, knowledge-lord, world-shiva.
Thus in those five and six sheaths, by turning of that, position revolves; indeed the endless god is in every way in the middle.
By the pair of six upper and lower skull sheaths, by turning of that, pervaded in the middle by eight directional ones, the knot stated in Matanga scripture.
In the Sri Sara teaching, again this is declared as six sheaths; this knot-principle is the work of maya, then maya.
The maya principle is indeed pervasive, deep, formless, place of all dissolution; there world-division is not fit, that knot therefore.
The endless lord of maya principle simultaneously agitates collected atoms; she produces night by endless own enclosures.
By that, the declared veil net from kala to earth end is countless and various; maya alone is one and to be distinguished.
It is said in the Sri prior scripture: the earth-manifest pair is countless, called night-power, but one-natured.
Bonds previously said, om-syllables, five-eight, sage's family and womb, speech-goddess; one born in her is not born again.
At initiation time, in earth-path purification, all that goes the earth path of the endless is fully established near him.
Accomplishable, giver, subduer, meditator, ash: five dots, with formation, marked by five-meaning secret rudra goad heart.
Attraction and mirror, this eight of measures; all with unlost powers are authorities of maya principle.
Those with maya bodies enjoy their own enjoyment; at the end of dissolution, indeed by the endless, they are withdrawn, but at day's beginning.
By the grace of another endless, even wise ones think the supreme asleep-awakened, dull with self-will opinion.
Those situated in the maya interval know only their own self as cause; therefore maya goddess stands supreme, deluding creatures.
She is the power of the god of gods, doing very difficult things, obstructing without enmity; by her minds are made to wander.
Disputants here dispute this principle, this not-this; those not devoted to guru, deva, agni scriptures are lowest men.
Abandoning the true path, it certainly leads them to the false path, those clinging to dry logic.
Maya indeed deludes them in non-liberation, with desire for liberation; thus cut by the sword of shiva initiation and the sword of shiva knowledge.
No other cause sprouts again; cutting is directed toward it, and pure great knowledge stands above great maya.
Vageshvari stands there in the city of nine, including Vama, Jyeshtha, Raudri, Kali, Kalavikarani, Balavikarika, and others.
Mathani, Damani, Manonmani, and all those yellow powers amount to seven crores of chief mantra powers established in the knowledge principle.
Here there are lotus-shaped cities, seven knowledge queens beginning with triguna, and seven arbuda lords.
Above the knowledge principle is the aisha principle, ascending in order from Shikhanda to Ananta, joined with eight cities.
Shikhanda, Shrigala, Murti, one-eye, one-rudra, highest Shiva, subtle Rudra, Ananta, and the eight Vidyeshvaras are named.
In the ascending upward placement of the seven, Ananta is the leader and lord, to be meditated and worshipped increasingly.
Three crores are established with the chief mantra lords; these leaders are thereby Vidyeshas and world rulers.
The gurus said this in the Shiva-body teachings: a god with eight shakti pairs sits on the guha throne.
From the deep beginning to the end of hell, he creates, assigns Rudras, and uplifts men through Manonmani, remaining middle-standing.
Those uplifted by him enter supreme principle contemplation; he is again appointed by Shiva among path dwellers and atoms.
After the completed lord assignment, Ananta lord enters that abode with many soul mantra crores, while subtle Rudra extinguishes.
The lord establishes the first atom in Shikhanda's place; thus eight proceed in order until the abodes, by the single guru.
Those eight, seated on lotus thrones with eight shakti yoga, make liberation for countless beings.
They behold the god dwelling in the heart, the supreme cause Ananta, meditating on the peaceful cause in their own heart.
Seven crores of pure mantras meditate, extending from Maya to sun ray; becoming is called non-becoming beginning with Ananta.
This end of Shiva pure quality authority is also rejected here, because the appointability of the seen and granted is Shaiva.
Desired cessation is non-becoming below, but it does not become so, because it departs from the lord; causality and effecthood come from the accomplished.
In Shiva accomplishment like armor, the extreme and middle-standing pair is named, and the city of four—dharma, knowledge, dispassion, and mastery—is identified.
In this Ishvara principle, the form covering is known; Vama, Jyeshtha, and Raudri adorn the three worlds.
The subtle covering in the Isha principle, named by the best gurus, runs from Aisha to Sadashiva and is adorned with the knowledge-action pair.
The pure covering is thus said; from it comes the supreme, and then the knowledge covering shines with two powers of being and non-being.
The power covering, called measure, is determined in scripture; it is adorned by Tejasvi and Dhruvesha.
The Tejasvi covering is followed by the measure covering, which is adorned with three pure covering cities.

tokens.quick_gloss: above the Shiva-covering they call it named the liberation-covering

quick_english: Above the very-pure covering there is a single Shaiva city. Above the Shiva-covering, they say, lies the covering called the liberation-covering.

tokens.quick_gloss: but above the liberation-covering a single-city covering

quick_english: In this liberation-covering, eleven Rudras are described. Above the liberation-covering there is a single-city covering called the fixed one.

tokens.quick_gloss: above the fixed covering the will-covering
dwelling inside the house of the Lord's will, that city
and is said to be one

quick_english: Above the fixed covering is the will-covering. There dwell those Shivas inside the house of the Lord's will, and that city is said to be one.

tokens.quick_gloss: frequented by the eight directional Rudras

quick_english: Above the will-covering is the one called the awakened covering, frequented by the eight directional Rudras. Above the awakened covering lies the great covenant-covering.

tokens.quick_gloss: enclosing within it the covering of Ananta by five
above the covenant-covering the auspicious-Shiva realm

quick_english: The covenant-covering encloses the covering of Ananta within five worlds. Above it lies the auspicious-Shiva realm, and there is the great world called Sadakhya.

tokens.quick_gloss: the power resting in his lap

quick_english: In that world dwells the god Sadashiva. His powers of knowledge and action are on his left and right, while his supreme will rests in his lap.

tokens.quick_gloss: the five acts beginning with creation
Brahmas and the group of six limbs
the group of eight beginning with Sakala

quick_english: By that will, Sadashiva performs the five acts beginning with creation. With him are the five Brahmas, the six limbs, the group of eight beginning with Sakala, and other Shivas.
The auspicious Shiva is surrounded by those ten and eighteen Rudras. The five Brahmas are Sadyojata, Vama, Aghora, Purusha, and Ishana, and the heart is named among them.

tokens.quick_gloss: head, tuft, armor, eye, and weapon as limbs

quick_english: They declare the six limbs to be head, tuft, armor, eye, and weapon, together with the heart. Along with them are Sakala, Akala, Shunya, Kaladhya, Kha, and Kshapana as the last.

tokens.quick_gloss: the throat-and-lip one as the eighth
this group of eight Saktalas is transmitted

quick_english: The throat-and-lip one is the eighth, and this group of eight Saktalas is traditionally transmitted. Then are named Omkara, Shiva, Dipta, Hetu, Isha, Dasheshaka, Sushiva, and Kala.
Sukshma, Sutejas, and Sharva are these ten Shivas. Then, beginning from the east, come Vijaya, Nihshvasa, Svayambhuva, Vahni, Vira, and Raurava.

tokens.quick_gloss: Mukuta, Visara, Indu, Bindu, and Prodgita

quick_english: Mukuta, Visara, Indu, Bindu, Prodgita, Lalita, Siddha, Rudra, Santana, Shiva, Para, Kirana, and Paramesha are remembered as the Rudras.

tokens.quick_gloss: having names equal to their own
joined with Vibhu, Vama, and the Rudras and their powers

quick_english: All these Rudras have knowledges that bear names equal to their own. They are surrounded by crores of mantra-sages and joined with Vibhu, Vama, and the Rudras together with their powers.

tokens.quick_gloss: endowed with Tara and other powers
the seat of Sushiva as a very white lotus with countless petals

quick_english: Sushiva's seat is a very white lotus with countless petals, endowed with Tara and other powers. The group of powers and Rudras is present both in his retinue and on his seat.

tokens.quick_gloss: freed from the impurity of maya

quick_english: In each one's own retinue there are countless crores beyond measure. They are freed from the impurity of maya, yet remain established only in their office.

tokens.quick_gloss: when the bondage of office dissolves

quick_english: In the covering of Sushiva, the Rudras are all-knowing and full of all powers. When the bondage of their office dissolves, they become peaceful, take on the form of Shiva, and are no longer subject to rebirth.

tokens.quick_gloss: adorned by resting in the lap of his power

quick_english: Above is the radiant covering of bindu. There is a moon-bright lotus, and there Shiva as Shantyatita is adorned, resting in the lap of his power.

tokens.quick_gloss: surrounded by the retinue of the kala group beginning with Nivritti
surrounded by crores of cities of countless Rudras and their powers

quick_english: He is surrounded by the retinue of the kala group beginning with Nivritti, and by crores of cities of countless Rudras and their powers.
In the revered Matanga scripture, the highest principle called Laya is, by that technical name, identified here with bindu.

tokens.quick_gloss: that which is with parts and without parts

quick_english: That bright principle, made of four forms and both with parts and without parts, is where enjoyment is said to take place. This is how it is described here.

tokens.quick_gloss: because of Nivritti and the rest
because of extreme subtlety, embodiment beginning from earth is not formed
because of absorption in flashing great knowledge, not

quick_english: Because Nivritti and the other kalas are extremely subtle, embodiment beginning from earth does not take shape in the usual way. Since the Mother is absorbed in flashing great knowledge, it is not distinctly perceived.

tokens.quick_gloss: appear, so too those in the bodies of the higher and lower Rudras

quick_english: Just as earth particles in gold do not appear separately because its fiery nature predominates, so too the elements in the bodies of the higher and lower Rudras do not appear separately.

tokens.quick_gloss: above bindu is the half-moon; of that
are the obstructing powers; from that

quick_english: Above bindu is the half-moon. From that come kala, moonlight, radiance, splendor, and the pure one. These five are the obstructing powers.

quick_english: Rodhikā blocks the causal lords beginning with Brahma; one should abandon it. Then, after piercing this nirodhikā, one reaches the supreme world called Sadakhya.

quick_english: There, in supreme form, abides the one whose great body is made of the five mantras. Thus, above the covering of bindu that ends in the half-moon and nirodhi, there is a great presence.
Nāda is like the filaments of a flower and is surrounded by great beings. There are four worlds in the directions and a fifth in the center.
Indhikā, Dīpikā, Rodhikā, and the upward-going Mocikā are there. In the middle is a lotus, and there the upward-moving one is surrounded by its powers.

quick_english: Above nāda is the suṣumna realm. There the lord who bears its powers is surrounded on the left and right by Piṅgalā and Iḍā.
The goddess Suṣumnā, resting in the lord's lap and shining like the moon, strings together the whole path, both above and below.

tokens.grounds: but the support of nāda and suṣumnā

quick_english: The support of nāda and suṣumnā pierces this entire universe; it goes out below by the downward power and above from the crown by the upward power.
Absorbed through the channel in the cavity of Brahma, that unmanifest, resonant, imperishable sound resounds in all beings, empowered by Śiva's śakti.

tokens.grounds: the covering known as the brahma cavity

quick_english: Above Suṣumnā is the covering called the brahma cavity. There dwells Brahmā, white, three-eyed, bearing a trident, five-faced, and crowned with the moon.

tokens.grounds: moving on the path of liberation

quick_english: In his lap sits the supreme goddess Brahmāṇī, who moves on the path of liberation and both obstructs and grants release. Piercing through her, one comes to the upward Kuṇḍalinī.
That śakti is like a sleeping serpent and is called the support of the universe. Within her are the subtle, the very subtle, Amṛtā, Amitā, and other powers.
In the middle is Vyāpinī, and within her is Vyāpīśa, the bearer of Vyāpinī. This is the śakti principle, whose manifestation extends all the way down to earth.

tokens.grounds: the sky-natured Ananta lord and those sharing his śaktis

quick_english: Then comes the Śiva principle. Established in the four directions are Vyāpī, the sky-natured lord Ananta, and those who share in his powers.

tokens.grounds: bearing its śakti in his lap, radiant like a hundred crore suns

quick_english: In the middle there is the unsupported one: the god of gods, Anāśrita, bearing his śakti in his lap and shining with the radiance of a hundred crore suns.
Above the Śiva principle is the supreme śakti called Samanā. She abides as the active agent of all causes.
Empowered by Śiva, she bears many cosmic eggs. Resting upon her, Lord Śiva performs the five acts.

tokens.grounds: of the causal agent, the great lord

quick_english: Samanā is the instrument of that great causal lord. The unsupported principle, in activity, is the occasioning cause and is called the cause.
Through her the all-pervading lord presides over the five causes. This unsupported, lordly, endless, sky-bodied one does so always.
He impels the pervading lord by his own śakti as instrument. Below that abides Māyā in the form of karma, and below that is the śakti Kuṇḍalinī.
